dramatic.state_in: Greg is becoming predictably present at theatre.
dramatic.required_result: Show belonging through spatial accommodation and tiny utility rather than invitation or praise.
dramatic.state_out: Greg realizes his presence now affects sightlines, work traffic, and casual requests.
dramatic.ownership: Theatre people own workspace; Greg owns moving when told; belonging remains emergent.

performance.behavior: Teren redirects Greg's chair because he blocks sightlines; workers say foot or crutch as ordinary traffic instructions; Greg holds pages and identifies a prop letter.

screenplay: Greg arrives and is greeted by name.
Teren redirects his usual chair because Greg's predictable presence affects sightlines.
Workers tell him foot and crutch as they pass, trusting him to adjust.
Teren hands him pages because his hand is full.
A prop-letter mix-up reaches Greg; he identifies the merchant letter.
A worker thanks Gregory and rehearsal continues.

dramatic.state_in: Internal shaping control is improving; external effect remains unproven.
dramatic.required_result: Run a first bounded external extension test with baseline confounds observed beforehand.
dramatic.state_out: The thread moves once during REACH, attribution unknown; Greg demonstrates good control by not chasing it.
dramatic.ownership: Hessa owns apparatus/interpretation; Greg owns sensation/compliance.

performance.pressure: The smallest visible external event carries huge emotional weight.
performance.behavior: Hessa proves the thread moves for ordinary reasons before magic; Greg reports heart rate, breathes normally, and obeys no-more instructions after movement.
performance.relationship: Allowing the external question itself shows Hessa's trust.

screenplay: Hessa unveils a thread three-quarters of an inch from Greg's forearm and denies broader clearance.
They establish baseline movement from breathing and room conditions.
Greg draws and shapes a localized forearm region.
On REACH the altered region becomes asymmetric toward the thread and the thread moves toward his arm once.
Greg freezes emotionally, not magically; Hessa tells him to hold.
A repeat inside the same attempt does not move it. They record observed movement with unknown cause.

dramatic.state_in: Greg has an ambiguous external result and two required living days.
dramatic.required_result: Let ordinary time with Lyssa keep ambiguity from becoming obsession.
dramatic.state_out: Greg can say he does not know and choose companionship over immediate investigation.
dramatic.ownership: Lyssa owns companionship; Hessa owns future tests; Greg owns waiting.

performance.pressure: The magic result wants to consume the scene.
performance.behavior: Lyssa hears the thread story, recognizes the uncertainty as awful, then holds Greg's hand without making it evidence. Greg repeatedly catches himself scoring mundane observations.
performance.relationship: Lyssa's value is not solving him.

screenplay: Lyssa catches Greg selecting pears and steals one.
They navigate market obstacles with small corrections, no ceremony.
At a fountain Greg starts turning a child's hoop failures into a system and stops himself.
He tells Lyssa the thread moved but maybe not because of him.
She holds his hand and asks what he will do today.
Greg chooses to stay there with her.

dramatic.state_in: Greg is comfortable enough at theatre to interfere with a prop problem.
dramatic.required_result: Teach that illusion can work through combined timing even when components are crude.
dramatic.state_out: Greg accepts sufficient function over a technically better repair because the scene already has horse.
dramatic.ownership: Theatre owns stage effect; Greg owns repair quality only if repair is still needed.

performance.pressure: Greg sees a solvable defect and assumes solving remains relevant.
performance.behavior: The company runs through a broken hoof board by improvising sound; Greg fabricates a good peg and discovers the solution has been bypassed.
performance.relationship: Theatre keeps stealing Greg's problems by continuing to function.

screenplay: A servant actor makes a terrible horse noise because the hoof board is missing.
The board plus a gray cloth flash creates a fake but legible horse.
The board breaks; rehearsal keeps going using box slaps and mouth clicks.
Greg makes a replacement peg.
A spare cup is already tied on with cord when he returns.
Worker: we have horse. Greg puts the better peg in the repair box.

dramatic.state_in: One external thread movement was ambiguous.
dramatic.required_result: Use a second thread as room comparison while keeping internal control stable.
dramatic.state_out: A differential near-thread movement improves interpretability without proving causation.
dramatic.ownership: Hessa owns claims; Greg owns technical questions and subjective control.

performance.pressure: Greg understands controls well enough to overvalue them.
performance.behavior: Hessa demonstrates controls can differ without magic; Greg performs cleanly and RETURNs instead of chasing movement.
performance.relationship: Hessa lets Greg help think about apparatus after he respects attempt boundaries.

screenplay: Hessa hangs near and far threads and deliberately creates door/window/vibration baseline differences.
Greg calls the second thread a control; Hessa agrees but rejects truth-machine thinking.
During REACH near thread moves toward his arm while far does not at that moment.
Greg RETURNs and releases cleanly.
Afterward the far thread moves under ordinary room influence.
The result is improved confidence in interpretability, not mana causation.
